transcript:
00:00 Alex (Redwood): Hey everyone thanks for hopping on, uh we got about 45 minutes together, we wanted to show the new per route finance dashboard in the console. Priya can you confirm goals quickly?
00:08 Priya (Orthosys): Yep, main thing is we need clear chargeback for product teams — what each API route costs per month and per thousand requests, and also tie that back to model variants. We also have procurement questions about private deployments.
00:20 Marcus (Orthosys): And we need something that our finance team can consume; CSV export is non-negotiable.
00:26 Alex: Totally. Samir will start the live console demo, I'll jump in on questions and pricing assumptions.
00:32 Samir (Redwood): Alright I'm sharing my screen, give me a sec, ok this is the Console home. You can see top-level usage, but let's switch to the routes view.
00:45 Samir: Up top we have filters — time range, team tags, and model variant. If I select the last 30 days you get per-route spend and usage.
00:55 Jordan (Orthosys): That graph is nice, how is spend calculated? Is it purely token-based?
01:02 Samir: Good question. By default spend = tokens * model unit price + routing overheads. We also apply batching and KV cache savings where applicable. Side note, the KV cache sometimes shows up as K V cash in transcripts heh, but the console shows exact cache hits on the route.
01:17 Priya: Do you include streaming overheads? Some of our routes use streaming responses.
01:22 Samir: Yes, streaming has a per-request overhead plus per-token. You'll see an itemized breakdown if you click into a route. I'll open the sample route 'chat-support' — here: summary header, cost per 1k requests, avg latency, and cost by component.
01:36 Samir: Notice the 'Cost Attribution' tab, we break down by model variant (gpt-like vs open weights), infrastructure tier (hosted vs dedicated), and batching efficiency.
01:47 Marcus: Can you tag routes to teams? We have many microservices that call the same endpoint.
01:52 Samir: Yep — tags and route aliases. You can map HTTP paths or logic gates to a route. Later you can roll those tags up to cost centers.
02:04 Alex: Also worth noting is you can export the raw per-route ledger as CSV and map it to your internal billing numbers.
02:12 Priya: Show us an example export please.
02:15 Samir: Export button — CSV includes timestamp, route id, request id, model version, tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_component, cost_usd. I'll trigger an export now (download kicked off).
02:30 Evan (Orthosys): Nice, does that include PII masking? We sometimes log user messages for debugging.
02:36 Samir: We only include request metadata in exports. Payloads are redacted unless you enable retention for debug and opt-in to export payloads. For compliance we have KMS-backed encryption and audit logs.
02:49 Priya: On encryption, do you support customer-managed keys?
02:52 Alex: Yes, for Private and Dedicated we support KMS/HSM integrations. Hosted customers can opt into BYOK in our enterprise plan.
03:00 Jordan: What about SSO and RBAC? We need SCIM provisioning.
03:04 Alex: SCIM and SAML are supported, RBAC with least privilege roles, and audit trails for all admin actions.
03:12 Marcus: Back to the spend calc — can you show a scenario where batching reduces cost?
03:18 Samir: Sure. I'll switch the demo to the 'optimize' overlays. Here you can simulate batching and see projected savings. For this sample route you can see 22% token-savings via prefix caching and a 15% cost drop via batching.
03:34 Priya: That assumes similar payload shapes right? Our chats have variable lengths.
03:38 Samir: Correct, we use a traffic mix you provide to make accurate forecasts. For now it's a synthetic mix.
03:44 Alex: We'll need your distribution of seq lengths to make the pilot numbers realistic.
03:48 Priya: We'll add that to the CSV.
03:51 Samir: Also note model selection: you can route low-latency critical routes to dedicated lower-quantized models, and cheaper non-critical ones to hosted open models. The Console's route policy editor lets you set fallbacks and cost thresholds.
04:08 Marcus: Is routing by policy automated? Like if dedicated capacity hits threshold, will requests fall back automatically?
04:14 Samir: Yes — automatic fallback to compatible variants by policy. And you can prefer low-cost variants during off-peak windows.
04:21 Jordan: Any visibility for token-level breakdown across a conversation? We need to reconcile invoices back to conversation ids.
04:27 Samir: We surface per-request token counts and conversation ids in the ledger. If you use our SDK traces, we embed route and conversation metadata to make reconciliation straightforward.
04:39 Priya: Security review will want SOC2 artifacts and penetration test results.
04:44 Alex: We'll send the security pack after this call. It's in the next steps.
04:48 Evan: For pilot, can we provision a VPC-based private deployment?
04:52 Alex: Yes, pilot options include hosted sandbox, dedicated reserved capacity, or a private VPC deployment if you have strict data residency. There are tradeoffs on setup time and cost.
05:03 Marcus: What is the rough lead time for a private deployment?
05:06 Alex: Typically 4-8 weeks depending on network approvals and HSM setup. Dedicated reserved pools are faster, 2-3 weeks.
05:14 Priya: For chargeback we'd like per-team dashboards. Can we embed the Console views in our internal portal?
05:19 Samir: We have embeddable widgets and an API to pull per-route metrics; many customers use our direct CSV exports plus an API for live dashboards.
05:27 Jordan: Can we set budget alerts by route?
05:30 Samir: Yes — per-route SLOs and budget alerts. You can trigger webhooks when a route crosses thresholds.
05:36 Priya: Great. Can you show the drift/regression alerting for quality vs cost? We need to guard against quantization harming quality.
05:44 Samir: There's a quality monitoring panel tied to prompt sets — you can pin evals and get regression alerts if quality drops beyond a threshold after a rollout.
05:52 Marcus: If we pin a model version, can we still route some traffic to an experimental variant?
05:56 Samir: Yep — canary and A/B rollout controls per route. The Console will show comparative cost and quality metrics side-by-side.
06:07 Priya: For billing, can you break down the invoice by cost center automatically?
06:12 Alex: You can auto-apply tags for cost centers and generate a chargeback report monthly. It maps our ledger to your accounting codes.
06:20 Evan: Any examples of what finance teams liked?
06:22 Alex: We recently shipped a sample ledger-to-invoice mapping template; I'll send that.
06:28 Priya: About noise in transcription — haha — but seriously, what about observability for failed requests? We need to tie errors to cost spikes.
06:36 Samir: Error rate panels are aligned with spend; you can slice spend by error type. For example, repeated retries can balloon token counts and you'll see that as anomaly.
06:46 Jordan: Do you keep raw request logs long enough for audits?
06:49 Alex: Retention is configurable; for compliance customers we support extended retention with paid add-ons.
06:56 Marcus: Let's talk numbers — show a quick per-route example.
07:00 Samir: Example route 'billing-check' — 120k reqs last month, avg tokens 150 in + 200 out, total cost $3,600. If we enable caching and batch at 5 reqs, projected cost falls to $2,850. Here's the breakdown: base token cost, infra overhead, and optimization savings.
07:20 Priya: That helps. What assumptions on token pricing are you using?
07:24 Alex: We showed a blended price in the demo. For a pilot we'll lock in model/unit prices and show line-item math.
07:31 Marcus: If we run Dedicated reserved capacity, do we get lower per-token rates?
07:35 Alex: Yes, reserved commitments drop unit price and give predictable throughput; the console will let you model committed vs on-demand.
07:44 Priya: How do you measure caching savings? Do you dedupe identical prompts?
07:49 Samir: We do prefix caching and KV cache for repeated context, and we can also do similarity-based caching for embeddings where appropriate.
07:57 Evan: Any limits on CSV size exports? Our month is huge.
08:01 Samir: Exports are chunked and stored; for very large exports we provide a signed URL to download from S3.
08:08 Priya: Can the Console show amortized GPU cost per route?
08:12 Samir: We show infra allocation cost in the chargeback view. For Dedicated you can amortize GPU cost across routes and set custom cost allocation keys.
08:22 Marcus: Does Console support multi-region rollups for global services?
08:26 Samir: Yes, region-level and cross-region rollups with currency conversion.
08:31 Alex: Okay quick pause — any blockers so far?
08:34 Priya: Only that we need more accurate numbers based on our traffic. We'll share CSV.
08:38 Jordan: Also want security docs.
08:40 Alex: We'll attach those.
08:43 Samir: Back to the Console — here's the anomaly detection timeline. If a route's cost per request spikes, you'll see a flagged event and suggested actions like throttle, route to cheaper variant, or increase cache TTL.
08:58 Marcus: That's useful. Can the system propose optimized batching parameters automatically?
09:02 Samir: In Optimize we surface recommended batch sizes and quantization settings with projected cost and latency tradeoffs. You can then apply them to a route or simulate first.
09:13 Priya: How does quantization affect quality? We saw some artifacts in our internal experiments.
09:17 Samir: We recommend evals tied to your prompt set; Optimize shows expected regression risk and target latency gain. You can set guardrails to block deployment if quality drops too much.
09:30 Evan: Pilot timeline question again — what do you need from us to start a 2-week pilot?
09:35 Alex: Sample traffic mix CSV, route mapping, and credentials for a sandbox project. We'll provision demo env and seed it with your traffic.
09:42 Priya: We'll get that by Wednesday.
09:44 Alex: Great. Any compliance concerns?
09:46 Priya: Just BYOK and SOC2 report.
09:49 Alex: Noted.
09:51 Samir: I'm going to show how the route policy editor handles fallbacks — quick live edit: change fallback to open-model-1, save, and you can watch simulated traffic switch.
10:07 Marcus: Nice, does that trigger a rollout event that we can audit?
10:10 Samir: Yes it creates an audit entry with before/after and rollout percentage.
10:15 Priya: Can we hook into Slack for alerting?
10:18 Alex: Webhooks and native Slack integration available for alerts and monthly summaries.
10:24 Jordan: About billing classification — can the Console map routes to internal GL codes?
10:28 Samir: You can map route tags to GL codes and export a reconciled ledger.
10:33 Priya: For our finance team, do you provide sample chargeback report templates?
10:37 Alex: Yes, we'll send a sample mapping template and an example invoice.
10:42 Samir: One more thing: the console also surfaces 'wasted tokens' where retries or error flows consumed tokens but produced no business value. You can filter those out of billing in chargeback reports.
10:58 Marcus: That's great. Ok wrapping up — what's the immediate next step?
11:03 Alex: I'll send the pricing sheet and security pack, Samir will run the baseline with the shape you provide, and Priya will share the CSV. Then we schedule pilot kickoff for next week.
11:14 Priya: Works for us. Thanks everyone.
11:17 Alex: Thanks, we'll follow up by email with links and it's been recorded.
11:20 (crosstalk, end)
notes: Transcript includes some auto-generated sections. Minor transcription errors present (product names and acronyms). Conversation focused on per-route cost attribution, tagging, secure deployment options (KMS/BYOK), and pilot planning. Recording available in CRM link.
